rooms.4400: A lightless nothing presses in on every side, with no floor to feel and no wall to lean on. Cold and stillness are all there is, and even your own heartbeat sounds muffled and far away. Whatever prayers once drew you toward this blackness have left no mark upon it, and no way out can be found.
rooms.4401: Before the great doors of the abandoned cathedral the paving is cracked and sunken, and lichen creeps up the broad steps. A tall pointed porch looms overhead, its carved saints worn faceless by weather. Back north lies the Concourse and the last smoke and noise of Garathorm, while a path curls away east and west around the cathedral's walls. The doors to the south stand ajar upon the dusty dark of the antechamber.
rooms.4403: The path runs tight beside the cathedral's flank, where flying buttresses lean over it and old yew boughs shut out the sky. Moss has turned the flagstones into a soft green carpet that muffles every step. West the way opens toward the cathedral's porch, and south it slips off along a shaded track under darker trees. A cold draught seeps out of the stonework beside you.
rooms.4405: Yews and black cypresses meet overhead, and the path beneath is only a strip of damp earth between tilted headstones. The light here is green and weak, and the air smells of wet leaves and old stone. North the path winds back toward the cathedral wall, while ahead to the south the leaning graves of the churchyard begin in earnest.
rooms.4408: Crooked headstones crowd the grass here, many of them sunk to their shoulders in the turf and wearing names that no one can read. A trodden path leads north under the trees, and the ground opens east into a rough field. More graves run on to the south and west in untidy rows. A wind picks at the dry grass with a sound like whispering.
rooms.4414: The graves give out here and rank meadow grass takes over, waist-high and grey with seed. North, an iron gate hangs shut in a hedge of thorn, chained fast and thick with creeper, and nothing beyond it can be seen. Back west the headstones of the churchyard lean together like gossips. The wind is steady across the open ground and carries a smell of turned earth.
rooms.4411: A cluster of table tombs squats in the long grass, their lids split by the roots of an old yew that twists up out of one of them. Moss greys every inscription, and the carved skulls on the corners have lost their faces. The yard climbs gently north to a wider stretch of graves, and a row of smaller markers runs off west. Dew never seems to leave the stone.
rooms.4410: Here the graves stand in tidy rows, though the rows have heaved and slumped until each stone points a different way. Iron railings, rusted to lace, fence off a few of the older plots. To the south rises the squat grey front of a mausoleum, its bronze door green with age. The grass is trampled flat along the path that leads to it.
rooms.4407: A broken angel kneels on a plinth at the heart of this corner of the yard, her wings snapped and her folded hands worn to stumps. Ivy has wound itself around her shoulders as though to hold her up. Graves stretch east and west of her, and the ground slopes down south toward the tombs. The sky above is a pale smear behind the bare branches.
rooms.4406: The cathedral's grey side wall rises close to the north here, streaked black where the gutters long ago gave up. Beneath it the graves are older and the stones lower, half swallowed by nettles. West stands a squat mausoleum with a heavy door set into its face, and the yard runs on east and south. A cold smell of wax drifts faintly from somewhere inside the church.
rooms.4404: A narrow strip of ground runs between the cathedral wall and the yard, closed in by buttresses and the dripping eaves. East a low arched door, its oak gone silver, leads into the cathedral itself. The path goes on north toward the front of the church, and south it opens among the graves. Weeds sprout in every crack of the paving, and the stones are slick with green.
rooms.4402: This is the cathedral's outer flank, where the path squeezes between the buttresses and a wall of dark ivy. Stained glass high above has lost most of its panes, and a few coloured shards still glint dully in the lead. East the way returns to the great doors, and south the path runs along the side of the church. Everything smells of damp stone and rotting leaves.
rooms.4421: A short vaulted passage connects the side door to the nave, its floor of black and white tiles gone dull under years of grit. Empty sconces line the walls, their iron arms crusted with old wax. West is the door to the outer path, and east the passage opens upon the great hall. A faint, cold, sweetish smell hangs in the stillness.
rooms.4422: You stand at the western edge of the great hall, where the pews begin. They lie in splintered ranks, toppled and heaped, with prayer-books rotted into grey pulp on the shelves. Ahead the nave runs on east, and the hall continues both north and south of here. Far above, the roof timbers vanish into a darkness that echoes with every scuff of your boots.
rooms.4418: Slim pillars rise from the dust-thick floor to a ceiling lost in gloom, and between them the fallen pews lie in drifts. A heavy door stands closed to the north, leading into the antechamber, and a narrow panelled door in the west wall is half hidden behind a toppled lectern. The hall opens east and south. Candle-wax, long dead, has run down the pillars in pale ridges.
rooms.4415: A low stone antechamber, cold as a cellar, where worshippers once shook the rain from their cloaks. A spiral stair of worn steps winds upward in the corner toward the galleries. East the room continues, and south a heavy door opens into the hall. Hooks line the walls for cloaks nobody will ever hang, and a thin line of dust marks the floor.
rooms.4416: This is the main entrance of the cathedral, a broad stone chamber with a high roof and a floor scattered with leaves blown in through the cracks. The great doors stand to the north, barred with tarnished iron and grey with cobweb. West and east the antechamber continues, and south the hall opens on its fallen pews. Holy-water stoups beside the doors are dry and cracked.
rooms.4417: A cramped end of the antechamber, where a stone font of dry, cracked marble stands against the wall. An iron-railed stair climbs up from the corner toward the galleries, its rail slick with grime. West the entrance chamber lies open, and south a door leads down into the hall. A single shaft of grey light falls through a crack in the roof.
rooms.4420: Along this side of the hall the pews stand in better order, though every one has sagged on rotten legs. Dust lies thick on the floor, unbroken by any print but your own. North a door leads back into the antechamber, and the hall runs on south and west. Somewhere far off a bell tolls once, faint and thin, and the silence swallows the echo.
rooms.4424: A heavy oak door in the east wall leads to the sacristy, its handle worn bright by long years of priestly hands. The pews here lie in a tangle against the wall where something once dragged them. The hall continues north, south and west of here. Rushlight stubs sit crusted in iron brackets, and the floor tiles show cracks wide as a thumb.
rooms.4433: The sacristy is a narrow room of cedar cupboards and a long vestment table, everything furred with dust. Stained cloth, once crimson and gold, hangs in rotting folds from open drawers. West is the door back to the hall, and a plain door to the south leads on to a back room. The air is thick with the smell of old incense gone sour.
rooms.4434: A small back room, bare but for a scarred table and a rack of empty candle-holders on the wall. The floor boards near the far corner have been pulled up, revealing a stair of rough stone that drops away into cold darkness. North lies the sacristy, and the stairwell leads down toward something older. The silence in here is absolute and watchful.

4454.description: Burial niches line the walls in rows, each narrow slot sealed with a flat slab and a name scratched in the lime. The air is cold and dry and carries a faint smell of old dust and older rot. A tunnel leads east, and the vault of the catacombs runs on south. Water drips somewhere in the dark, steady as a slow pulse.

4463.description: A low tunnel of fitted stone runs through the catacombs here, its ceiling close enough to touch. Burial niches line the walls at the height of your shoulders, some still holding a wrapped shape. To the north, a narrow door set in the wall leads to a stranger passage, while the tunnel runs on south, east and west. The floor is worn into a shallow trough by countless passing feet.

4466.description: Skulls line the walls from floor to ceiling, set in tight rows with their empty sockets watching the passage. The mortar between them has crumbled and the whole wall seems to lean toward you. A door to the south opens back into the main tunnel, and the bone tunnel goes on west. The cold here has a dry, papery quality, like a held breath.

4467.description: The bone tunnel bends here, its walls built of thigh-bones stacked like firewood and capped with rows of yellowed skulls. Grit and bone-dust crunch underfoot. A narrow way leads north toward a junction, and a low door opens south, while the passage you came by runs back east. Every breath tastes of lime and old, dry things.

4470.description: Three passages meet here in a cramped junction, the walls patterned in bone as a mason might lay brick. A heavy door of black oak stands in the east wall, its hinges red with rust, and a wide archway opens west into a long, low room of piled skulls. The way south leads back down the bone corridor. A pale chalk mark has been drawn on the lintel and rubbed half away.

4471.description: Narrow shelves line this storeroom from floor to ceiling, crowded with clay jars sealed in black wax and empty urns without lids. A strong smell of tallow and mildew lingers in the close air. The only way out is the door west, which opens upon the bone corridor. Cobwebs hang from the shelves like grey bunting.

4472.description: The ossuary is a long vault of stacked bones, thousands of them, sorted by kind into walls and pillars and tidy pyramids. Skulls gaze from every ledge and alcove, and a crown of finger-bones is set above the arch like a decoration. A door in the north wall is closed and heavy with iron bands, and the junction lies back east. The silence here is the loudest in the whole place.

4473.description: A small, square room of damp stone, plain after the bone-lined halls behind. A bare stone bench runs along one wall, and nothing else breaks the grey. Scratches mark the plaster beside the door, a tally that ends mid-stroke. The only way out leads south into the ossuary.

4468.description: A small chamber off the bone tunnel, hardly wider than a man with outstretched arms. The ceiling is so low that your head brushes the cold, damp stone. Someone has scratched crude marks into the wall, long rows of them, and then gone no further. A narrow door in the north wall leads back to the tunnel.

4455.description: The catacomb passage widens into a long chamber lined with burial niches, many of them broken open and their stone lids lying cracked on the floor. A cold current of air moves through the place, smelling of earth and old candle smoke. West the way leads into a plain tunnel, south the passage runs on, and above you a gap in the ceiling opens onto a hidden stair.

4465.description: A corner of the catacombs where the burial niches are stacked three high, their slabs carved with worn names and faded dates. A faint trickle of water runs down one wall and pools on the floor in a black, still mirror. North the passage returns to a wider chamber, and a tunnel leads west. The cold is bone-deep and utterly still.

4462.description: Four passages of fitted stone cross here beneath a low arched ceiling. Dust lies undisturbed in the corners, but the middle of the floor is scuffed in a curious wide band. North and south run narrow tunnels, east is a burial chamber, and west lies another. A dull iron ring is set in the ceiling, bearing nothing now.

4461.description: A straight, narrow tunnel, its walls built of grey brick that sweats a cold moisture. Small niches are cut into the masonry at intervals, each holding a tarnished lamp of black glass. The passage runs north to a crossing and south toward a larger gallery. Your footfalls come back from the dark ahead, always a moment late.

4456.description: The catacomb opens here into a hall of low arches, supported by thick stone piers carved with weeping faces. Between the piers the burial niches are choked with dust and the dust with cobweb. A passage leads north into a narrow tunnel, and south the hall ends at a junction of ways. A smell of old stone and cold wax hangs unmoving.

4457.description: Four ways meet in this junction hall, each framed by an arch of black stone. A door of studded oak stands to the south, and a plainer archway opens west into a vault, while a tunnel leads east and the catacomb passage runs north. Faded runes ring the ceiling in a circle too worn to read. The air is bitterly cold.

4458.description: A rough tunnel, narrower and more crudely cut than the catacombs it leaves. The walls here are bare stone, hacked out with picks and never dressed. A door stands in the north wall, bound in rusted iron, and the tunnel returns west to the junction. The floor slopes gently down, and the damp grows heavier.

4469.description: The tunnel opens into a cavern, its roof lost in blackness and its floor a litter of broken stone. Stalactites hang from above like rows of teeth, and a thin, cold wind moves through the dark. The only way out is the door to the south. Somewhere deep in the rock, water falls in a slow, steady dripping.

4460.description: A burial vault of fitted stone, its roof held up by four squat pillars and its floor inlaid with the names of the dead. Stone sarcophagi stand along the walls, their lids carved with robed figures whose faces are worn smooth. A junction opens to the north, and above, a narrow stair behind an iron door climbs toward the mausoleum. The air smells of sealed places.

4413.description: The mausoleum stands cold and hushed, its walls lined with marble plaques and its floor strewn with dead leaves blown in under the door. A stone coffin rests on a dais in the centre, its lid shifted a hand's breadth to one side. The door north opens upon the churchyard, and a hatch in the floor drops to the vault below. Cold seeps from the marble.

4459.description: This vault is older than the cathedral above it, rough-hewn and low, with the dead laid in stacked stone coffins that crowd the walls. Roots hang from the ceiling like pale hair. A door leads east to the junction, and a stair in the corner climbs toward the light of the mausoleum above. A dry rustling runs through the dark, though nothing stirs.

4412.description: A small, domed mausoleum, its walls bearing the names of a long-dead family in raised letters worn by many winters. Three empty stone coffins stand open in the middle of the floor. The way east leads out to the churchyard, and a trapdoor at your feet drops into the vault below. Weak daylight slants in, grey and thin.

4464.description: The catacomb passage ends here at a wall of bricked-up niches, each plastered over and marked with a single faded cross. The air is still and tastes of dust. The passage returns north, and a low tunnel leads east. Someone has set a line of tiny dry stones along the floor, a pattern no one living remembers.

4437.description: A narrow passage hidden behind the panelling, cut straight through the old foundations. The walls are bare stone, unpainted, and the air is dank. A door to the north is set into the rock, a stair climbs up into the church, and the passage continues west. Footprints in the dust have long since been covered by new dust.

4436.description: You are at the bottom of an old well, its walls of green-slimed stone rising out of reach into darkness. The floor is a shallow bed of silt, long since dry. A low opening in the wall leads out through a door behind you. Far above, the circle of the sky is no more than a pale coin.

4438.description: A cramped, winding passage running through the wall of the church, so narrow that your shoulders brush both sides. Cobwebs hang in thick curtains, and the stone is slick with condensation. The way leads north to a landing, and east it returns to the stair. Behind the panelling, muffled, the cathedral's emptiness seems to listen.

rooms.4443: A hidden landing behind the cathedral's panelling, where a narrow stair climbs up into the open air over the roof. Thin cracks of light show between the boards at your side, and dust drifts down in the beams. A hidden door east opens into the gallery, and the secret passage descends south. The air smells of tar and old timber.
rooms.4439: The gallery runs along the upper edge of the great hall, a balcony of dark wood with a carved balustrade splintered in places. Below, the ranks of ruined pews are barely visible in the gloom. The gallery goes on east toward the belfry stair and south toward a vast organ, and a hidden door in the west wall leads into the walls. A stair spirals down at your back.
rooms.4442: The belfry's timber stair rises overhead in a tight spiral, and from up above, the great bell's rope hangs in a slow, small sway. Wooden beams crowd close, scored with the marks of carpenters long dead. The gallery lies west and south of here, and the stair climbs up toward the bell. Now and then a faint, wooden creak answers from the dark.
rooms.4441: The gallery ends here in a corner of the church's upper floor, with narrow windows that let in grey slats of light. Dust lies thick on the rail, unmarked by any hand. The way north leads on toward the belfry stair, west to the organ, and a stair spirals down to the antechamber. The air tastes of cold wax and old paper.
rooms.4440: The huge organ towers here against the wall, its pipes of tarnished tin rising into the gloom like the trunks of a petrified wood. Its keys are yellowed and cracked, and a faded hymn-board still stands on the music desk. The gallery passes by to the north and east. A faint, hollow note breathes from the pipes whenever the draught moves.
rooms.4452: The great bell hangs in its oaken frame, green with age and dull with dust. Louvred openings in the walls let a cold wind whistle through, and the rope sways gently without a hand upon it. A narrow ledge runs out on either side onto the outside of the tower, east and west, and the stair descends below. The whole tower hums with the ghost of old tolling.
rooms.4453: You cling to the outer wall of the tower, where a narrow ledge of weathered stone runs beside the open belfry. Wind tugs at your clothes, and the graveyard and the grey countryside lie spread out far below. West the louvred opening of the belfry offers shelter, and a ladder of iron rungs descends toward the roof. Moss and dark streaks stain the stone.
rooms.4445: A steep roof of lichen-crusted slate slopes away on every side, with lead gutters choked by years of moss. Tufts of grass sprout in the valleys between the gables, and the wind sings thinly through the chimneys. The roof continues south and west, and a ladder of iron rungs rises up the tower wall behind you. Beyond the parapet the graves look small as seed.
rooms.4447: A flat stretch of lead roofing lies between two steep pitches, pocked and green and hot to the touch at midday. A square hatch of oak, bound with iron, is set into the leads and leads down into the church. The roof runs on north and south from here. A cold wind off the plains blows steadily, bringing a smell of rain.
rooms.4449: The roof ends against a stone parapet, its crenellations broken like bad teeth. Beyond the edge lies a drop to the churchyard, whose crooked stones seem to nod. The slates run back north and the ridge continues west. Rain has left black stains on every surface, and the lichen here is the colour of old rust.
rooms.4448: The slates are loose here, cracked and slipping, and a patch of rotting timber shows where part of the roof has given way. The wind whips round the stonework with a low moaning. You can go north along the ridge or east across the leads. Far across the valley, the city wall of Garathorm is a thin grey line on the horizon.
rooms.4446: A long valley of lead runs between two ridges of slate, thick with fallen leaves and blown dust. A cracked gargoyle crouches at the edge of the gutter, its snarl worn smooth by the rain. The ridge climbs north toward the tower, and the valley falls away south. Overhead the clouds drift slowly, grey on grey.
rooms.4444: You stand upon the roof where the tower rises, a squat block of stone with a rusted iron ladder bolted to its face. Below, a trapdoor of rotted planks covers a hidden stair. The roof stretches away east and south, and the iron rungs climb up toward the belfry. The wind is cold and tastes of soot and rain.
rooms.4451: A narrow ledge of weathered stone clings to the tower's outer face, with the iron ladder bolted beside it. Gusts press you against the wall, and loose mortar trickles down at each step. East an opening in the belfry offers a way inside, and the rungs lead down to the roof. The land far below is a patchwork of green and grey.
rooms.4435: A cramped spiral stair of wedge-cut stone winds through the thickness of the cathedral's wall, lit by nothing but a thin seam of daylight from above. The steps are hollowed with age, and the central pillar is carved with faint, spidery runes. Up above, a hatch leads to the roof, a stair descends into cold dark, and a door in the west wall opens on the great hall. The air smells of tar and dust.
rooms.4428: A small door in the east wall of the hall leads into the wall's hidden stair, its panels so cleverly cut that they pass for part of the stone. The pews here are stacked against one another, as though cleared away in a hurry. The hall runs on north, south and west. A faded tapestry hangs by a single corner above the door.
rooms.4431: This far corner of the great hall is hung with rotting banners, their stitching unravelled. A glitter breaks the gloom to the west, where the altar stands. North the hall continues along the wall, and the flagstones are polished by a faint shine. Dust lies here as thick as snowfall.
rooms.4430: The diamond altar stands at the heart of the great hall, a block of clear crystal as high as your waist, throwing cold light in every direction. Candle-stubs ring its foot in a melted crown, and the flagstones around it are scuffed by a thousand kneeling years. The hall opens north, east and west around it. A deep hush hangs here, as though the altar kept a vigil of its own.
rooms.4427: Here the nave widens before the altar steps, and the fallen pews lie in a litter of broken kneelers and splintered backs. Brass candlesticks, green and bent, lie among the wreckage. Light from the west and south catches the glitter of the altar beyond. The hall runs north, east and west, and the altar waits to the south.
rooms.4423: Directly above, the great rose window gapes broken, its tracery bare and spiked with the last coloured shards. Pale light falls through in slanted bars, picking out drifting dust. Here the hall runs in all four directions, between toppled pillars and heaped pews. A cold, slow draught circles in the nave.
rooms.4419: A round stone well-curb breaks the floor of the nave here, its iron cover long since rusted through and its dark throat open. A cold breath rises from it, smelling of old water and mud. The hall continues east, south and west of here, and the antechamber lies through a door to the north. Chains hang from a beam above the well like a dead creeper.
rooms.4426: The pews stand in ragged lines along this side, their kneelers gnawed by damp and time. A grey alcove opens in the west wall behind a curtain of cobweb, and the nave continues north, east and south. The flagstones are cracked by the roots of something that has found its way under the church. A smell of stale incense lingers.
rooms.4429: In a far corner of the hall, a great trapdoor of black oak has been wrenched half open, revealing a stair of slick stone plunging down. A raw cold pours up from it, smelling of earth and old bones. The hall runs north and east, and the stair leads down into the dark. Scratches on the flags mark where heavy things were dragged.
rooms.4425: A shallow alcove behind the pews, its back wall painted with a faded fresco of kneeling saints, their haloes flaked away to bare plaster. A stone bench runs along the wall, polished by the knees of long-dead penitents. The hall lies east. The air is musty and cold, and the paint dust crunches under foot.
rooms.4432: A hidden alcove, hardly more than a closet, built into the thickness of the wall behind the panelling. A narrow shelf holds an old stub of candle and a heap of crumbled parchment. Cold dust fills every corner, and the stone sweats. The only way out is the door east, leading back to the great hall.
rooms.4409: The graves here lie close together, their headstones fallen forward like a row of dominoes. A cracked urn on a pedestal stands stained and empty, and nettles grow thick where the wind has piled dead leaves. North, a line of older stones runs toward the cathedral wall, and east the yard continues past a sunken path. A sour smell of wet earth hangs in the shade.

4407.description: The kneeling angel's face is gone, chiselled flat by wind and rain. A faint line of letters runs along her plinth, but only the word 'rest' can still be made out.

4413.description: The stone coffin is carved with the likeness of a robed priest, his hands crossed upon his breast. The lid has been shoved aside, and something inside has been long since taken.

4423.description: The tracery of the rose window forms twelve great petals, now empty of almost all their glass. A few ruby and sapphire shards cling to the lead like dried petals.

4430.description: The altar is a single flawless crystal, uncut and faintly luminous, without a seam or a flaw. Its heart shows dark shapes, like figures in a frozen pool, and the cold it gives off stings the fingers.

4440.description: The pipes are tarnished and bent, some as thick as a man's body. Their mouths are choked with dust, but a breath of air still draws a low note from them.

4452.description: The bell is cast with a band of saints and a date too corroded to read. Its clapper has been tied back with rotted cord, yet now and then it stirs by itself.
